power.title: Power Analysis Check

table.text: Cluster-wide scan of imputed structural variants 11p15.5 contains repeat and structural variation that haplogroup tagging cannot reach, including the MUC2 VNTR domain. We therefore asked whether any common, well-imputed VNTR or structural-variant allele across the cluster (109 variants) is associated with IPF independently of rs35705950, recognising that this sample can only detect large effects. Twenty-one reached the cluster-wide threshold marginally, but all were attenuated by adjustment for rs35705950 and none reached it after adjustment (Supplementary Table S5). This is a power-limited negative. Taking the effect sizes and allele frequencies Kousathanas et al. report for the eight mucin-cluster 11p15.5 signals, this sample has 74% power to detect their most strongly associated MUC5B signal (OR 1.71 at a frequency of 0.20) at the cluster-wide threshold but 1% to 2% power for each of the four MUC2 and MUC6 signals, whose odds ratios are 1.15 to 2.10 at allele frequencies of 0.007 to 0.69 (Methods). The absence of those signals here is therefore uninformative.

text.text: Take-home message: In a dedicated IPF case-control study, the MUC5AC H3 and MUC5B H1 associations were not separable from the MUC5B promoter variant rs35705950.
A MUC5AC H2 association that did survive adjustment here was not replicated in a larger independent sample.
Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and frequently fatal fibrotic lung disease (Raghu et al., 2022).
text.formatted: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and frequently fatal fibrotic lung disease <ref type="bibr" target="#b13">(Raghu et al., 2022)</ref>.

text.text: The strongest common genetic risk factor is a gainof-function promoter variant in the mucin gene MUC5B (rs35705950; minor allele frequency ~9% in Europeans), whose minor (T) allele confers an odds ratio of approximately 4 per allele (Seibold et al., 2011; Allen et al., 2017) and explains an estimated 2-11% of variation in IPF risk against an overall heritability of 28% (Moll et al., 2023).
text.formatted: The strongest common genetic risk factor is a gainof-function promoter variant in the mucin gene MUC5B (rs35705950; minor allele frequency ~9% in Europeans), whose minor (T) allele confers an odds ratio of approximately 4 per allele <ref type="bibr">(Seibold et al., 2011;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b1">Allen et al., 2017)</ref> and explains an estimated 2-11% of variation in IPF risk against an overall heritability of 28% <ref type="bibr" target="#b9">(Moll et al., 2023)</ref>.

text.text: It increases MUC5B expression in the bronchiolar epithelium and is thought to predispose to fibrosis through mucociliary dysfunction (Seibold et al., 2011; Hancock et al., 2018) or epithelial cell stress (Dobrinskikh et al., 2023; Bridges et al., 2025).
text.formatted: It increases MUC5B expression in the bronchiolar epithelium and is thought to predispose to fibrosis through mucociliary dysfunction <ref type="bibr">(Seibold et al., 2011;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b5">Hancock et al., 2018)</ref> or epithelial cell stress <ref type="bibr" target="#b4">(Dobrinskikh et al., 2023;</ref> <ref type="bibr">Bridges et al., 2025)</ref>.

text.text: MUC5B and MUC5AC lie within the 11p15.5 mucin cluster and encode gel-forming mucins with large central variable number tandem repeat (VNTR) regions.

Plender et al. used long-read sequencing to define three MUC5AC haplogroups (H1 short, H2 medium, H3 long) and two MUC5B haplogroups (H1 less common, H2 common), with tagging SNPs (tSNPs) allowing assignment in short-read data (Plender et al., 2024).
text.formatted: Plender et al. used long-read sequencing to define three MUC5AC haplogroups (H1 short, H2 medium, H3 long) and two MUC5B haplogroups (H1 less common, H2 common), with tagging SNPs (tSNPs) allowing assignment in short-read data <ref type="bibr" target="#b11">(Plender et al., 2024)</ref>.

text.text: Both are phylogenetic clades from putatively neutral non-coding sequence, but the MUC5AC clades also differ in repeat length (H3 is ~670 amino acids longer than H1), whereas the MUC5B protein clades do not.
There are biological grounds to ask whether haplogroup matters beyond rs35705950.

The VNTR encodes the serine-and threonine-rich backbone carrying the O-glycans that set mucus viscoelasticity, and MUC5AC and MUC5B are the principal determinants of mucociliary clearance (Hill et al., 2022; Abrami et al., 2024).
text.formatted: The VNTR encodes the serine-and threonine-rich backbone carrying the O-glycans that set mucus viscoelasticity, and MUC5AC and MUC5B are the principal determinants of mucociliary clearance <ref type="bibr" target="#b6">(Hill et al., 2022;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b0">Abrami et al., 2024)</ref>.

text.text: VNTR structure could therefore act on that mechanism through protein architecture rather than expression.
Length is not the only route: clades differ in other architectural features and may carry regulatory or other coding variation.

At MUC5B, where length is essentially invariant in Europeans (Plender et al. report expanded VNTRs in seven haplotypes, all of African ancestry), any effect must be of that kind, which is the reason to test the MUC5B haplogroups despite their shared repeat length.
text.formatted: At MUC5B, where length is essentially invariant in Europeans <ref type="bibr">(Plender et al. report expanded</ref> VNTRs in seven haplotypes, all of African ancestry), any effect must be of that kind, which is the reason to test the MUC5B haplogroups despite their shared repeat length.

text.text: This has not been tested directly.

In the All of Us phenome-wide scan no MUC5AC haplogroup tag survived multiple-testing correction, and the MUC5B locus was represented by rs35705950 rather than a haplogroup tag (Plender et al., 2024).
text.formatted: In the All of Us phenome-wide scan no MUC5AC haplogroup tag survived multiple-testing correction, and the MUC5B locus was represented by rs35705950 rather than a haplogroup tag <ref type="bibr" target="#b11">(Plender et al., 2024)</ref>.

text.text: A genomewide tandem-repeat study in IPF reported an associated repeat at 11p15.5 that lost significance once rs35705950 was included, but its catalogue was restricted to repeat units of ≤20 bp, so it indexed a shorter intergenic repeat rather than the MUC5AC (24 bp) or MUC5B (87 bp) coding VNTRs, and it did not test the haplogroup classification (Oketch et al., 2025).
text.formatted: A genomewide tandem-repeat study in IPF reported an associated repeat at 11p15.5 that lost significance once rs35705950 was included, but its catalogue was restricted to repeat units of ≤20 bp, so it indexed a shorter intergenic repeat rather than the MUC5AC (24 bp) or MUC5B (87 bp) coding VNTRs, and it did not test the haplogroup classification <ref type="bibr" target="#b10">(Oketch et al., 2025)</ref>.

text.text: We therefore ask, in IPFJES (the IPF Job Exposures Study), a dedicated IPF case-control study (Reynolds et al., 2023), how much haplogroup association, if any, is independent of rs35705950.
text.formatted: We therefore ask, in IPFJES (the IPF Job Exposures Study), a dedicated IPF case-control study <ref type="bibr" target="#b14">(Reynolds et al., 2023)</ref>, how much haplogroup association, if any, is independent of rs35705950.

text.text: Tagging SNPs are the usual way to index these clades in array data, and such a test shows whether clade membership adds to the promoter variant, not which feature of a clade is responsible.
IPFJES is a multicentre UK case-control study of men, recruiting from 21 hospitals in England, Scotland, and Wales (Reynolds et al., 2023).
text.formatted: IPFJES is a multicentre UK case-control study of men, recruiting from 21 hospitals in England, Scotland, and Wales <ref type="bibr" target="#b14">(Reynolds et al., 2023)</ref>.

text.text: IPF cases were diagnosed at multidisciplinary team meetings by 2011 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT guidelines; recruitment ran from February 2017 to October 2019.
Controls were participants without IPF from the same centres, frequency-matched for age.
All participants provided written informed consent.
Ethical approval was granted by the East Midlands -Nottingham 1 Research Ethics Committee (REC 17/EM/0021; IRAS 203355).
Of 902 IPFJES participants with clinical data, 829 also had typed-array and imputed chromosome 11 genotypes with complete covariates.

One centre (n=31) enrolled cases only, so its centre indicator predicted case status perfectly and the corresponding coefficient could not be estimated (complete separation); that centre was excluded, leaving 798.

Because genetic ancestry is the principal confounder here and adjustment alone may not remove it, analyses were then restricted to participants of self-reported white ethnicity, who form a single genetic cluster: 25 of the 27 excluded lie beyond 3 SD of the whiteethnicity mean on PC1.
This gave an analytical sample of 771 participants (385 cases, 386 controls) used throughout, with principal components recomputed within it.
Participants were genotyped on the Biobank Affymetrix Axiom array (GRCh37).

As previously described (Chin et al., 2026), sample-level quality control removed individuals with low genotyping call rate (<95%), high heterozygosity, sex mismatches, duplicates, and high relatedness.
text.formatted: As previously described <ref type="bibr" target="#b3">(Chin et al., 2026)</ref>, sample-level quality control removed individuals with low genotyping call rate (<95%), high heterozygosity, sex mismatches, duplicates, and high relatedness.

text.text: Imputation used the TOPMed reference panel (GRCh38); imputed variants with r²<0.5 or minor allele count ≤3 were excluded.
text.formatted: Imputation used the TOPMed reference panel (GRCh38); imputed variants with r²<0.5 or minor allele count ≤3 were excluded.

text.text: We used a two-step procedure.
First, 17 MUC5AC tSNPs were extracted from our GRCh38 imputed data using PLINK v2: 16 of the 92 tags listed in Plender et al.
Supplementary Table S4, plus rs35779873 from their Table S6.

text.text: Second, one concordance SNP was chosen per haplogroup as the primary tag, the H3 and H2 tags entered as allele-dosage counts and H1 serving as the reference: H3 by rs28542750 (r²=1.0) and H2 by rs879201833 (r²=0.888, the best available H2 tag), with H1 as reference (the most common haplogroup, r²=0.899 for rs769768817).
The remaining 14 tSNPs were retained as a cross-check on those three (Supplementary Table S1).

Table S6 where listed, and otherwise by matching the counted-allele frequency in our controls to the published haplogroup frequency.

text.text: Plender et al. name the two concordance tSNPs in their main text but do not give their alleles, so those were oriented by frequency; rs35705950 was oriented by its established risk allele.
The direct H2 tag is primary because it tags H2 directly rather than by subtraction.
The joint model is therefore an approximate rather than exact H1-reference parameterisation.
Tags were cross-checked against 14 further tagging SNPs (Supplementary Table S1). Plender et al.'s main text transposes the haplogroup labels for rs28542750 and rs769768817 relative to Plender et al.

Smoking history and lifetime occupational history were collected at the same structured telephone interview, by an interviewer unaware of case status (Reynolds et al., 2023); ever-smoking and age were covariates in all models.

text.text: Occupational asbestos exposure was ascertained by Peto job-exposure matrix applied to the occupational history (binary classification); 502 of 771 participants (65.1%) were classified as exposed.

The replication sample comprised 1,961 IPF cases and 3,816 controls of European ancestry from the National Institutes of Health Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) programme, after restriction to participants with complete covariate data.

Cases were diagnosed according to American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society criteria at centres in the United States, Europe and Australia and underwent whole-genome sequencing through the TOPMed Whole Genome Sequencing in Familial and Sporadic Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis Study.

Controls were unaffected individuals aged 50 years or older selected from the TOPMed Genetic Epidemiology of COPD Study (COPDGene), TOPMed Framingham Heart Study (FHS) and TOPMed Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA).
All participants gave written informed consent under IRB-approved protocols for their parent studies.
No two participants were related at third degree or closer, and European ancestry was assigned using ancestry-informative principal components (Peljto et al., 2023).

MUC5B H1, MUC5AC H1 and MUC5AC H2 were inversely correlated with T count (r=-0.113, -0.140 and -0.235), so the risk allele co-occurs with the MUC5B H2 and MUC5AC H3 backgrounds.
Carrier status for H3 and for the T allele was nonetheless discordant in 241 of 771 participants (31%).

Only H3 has appreciable LD with rs35705950, and its estimate in the IPFJES controls (r²=0.10, slightly lower than the full-sample r² of 0.13 because cases are enriched for risk haplotypes) is consistent with the 1000 Genomes European reference (0.10; Supplementary Table S6), so the LD is representative rather than a feature of this cohort.

text.text: MUC5AC H3 was positively associated with IPF (OR 1.63, 95% CI 1.26-2.09; p=1.8×10⁻⁴), but not independently of rs35705950: adjusting for the promoter variant attenuated H3 to the null (OR 1.10, 95% CI 0.83-1.45; p=0.52), while rs35705950 itself retained a strong effect (OR 3.90, 95% CI 2.83-5.38; p=1.1×10⁻¹⁶).

Each additional MUC5B H1 copy, in place of H2, was associated with lower odds of IPF (OR 0.71, 95% CI 0.52-0.98; p=0.038), and this likewise attenuated after adjustment (OR 0.82, 95% CI 0.58-1.15; p=0.25).

The three-haplotype joint model (H1 reference) showed the same pattern for H3, but a MUC5AC H2 association persisted after additional adjustment for rs35705950, each additional H2 copy in place of H1 being associated with lower odds of IPF (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.51-0.94; p=0.017, which does not survive correction for the four primary coefficients).

This estimate was stable across tag choices, agreeing with the three panel H2 tSNPs and with the diplotype complement, that is, H2 count inferred by subtraction from the other two haplogroups (2 -H1 -H3) rather than from a tag of its own (Supplementary Table S3).

text.text: Genotypic fits for H3 and H2 did not improve on the additive model (Supplementary methods).
The same models were fitted in the TOPMed IPF case-control sample (1,961 cases, 3,816 controls; adjusted for sex, age, smoking and PC1-4), with haplogroups assigned from the same tags and coding.
The MUC5AC H3 findings replicated: OR 1.62 (95% CI 1.47-1.78) unadjusted in TOPMed against 1.63 (1.26-2.09) here (p=0.96 for heterogeneity).

In both samples the association was abolished by adjustment for rs35705950, falling to 0.94 (0.84-1.05) in TOPMed and 1.10 (0.83-1.45) here (p=0.31 for heterogeneity); neither adjusted interval excludes 1, so this is attenuation to the null rather than a reversal of direction.

H2 is estimable only alongside H3, with H1 as reference, so the estimate before adjustment for rs35705950 is the H3-adjusted one: 0.83 (0.74-0.93) in TOPMed against 0.58 (0.43-0.78) here (p=0.028 for heterogeneity).

The rs35705950-adjusted H2 residual, however, did not replicate: it was null in TOPMed (OR 0.99, 0.88-1.11), an interval that excludes the 0.69 (0.51-0.94) estimated here, in a sample with five times as many cases.
Because IPFJES recruited men only, the TOPMed models were refitted separately by sex (adjusted for age, smoking and PC1-4).

The pattern was the same in both: H3 was associated with IPF before adjustment for rs35705950 (men 1.68, 1.48-1.90; women 1.40, 1.19-1.65) and null after it (1.01, 0.88-1.17; 0.85, 0.70-1.02), and the H2 residual was null in both (1.00, 0.87-1.16; 0.97, 0.79-1.19).
The failure of the H2 association to replicate is therefore not explained by the maleonly composition of IPFJES.
The MUC5B H1/H2 discriminator failed quality control in TOPMed, so the MUC5B association could not be tested there.
The samples differ in composition.
A higher proportion of TOPMed controls than TOPMed cases had ever smoked (73.9% versus 68.7%), the reverse of the pattern in IPFJES (69.7% of controls versus 75.8% of cases).
TOPMed controls came from the COPDGene, Framingham and MESA cohorts.
IPFJES recruited men only, and its controls were patients attending outpatient clinics, so neither control group represents the general population.
Cluster-wide scan of imputed structural variants 11p15.5 contains repeat and structural variation that haplogroup tagging cannot reach, including the MUC2 VNTR domain.

We therefore asked whether any common, well-imputed VNTR or structural-variant allele across the cluster (109 variants) is associated with IPF independently of rs35705950, recognising that this sample can only detect large effects.
Twenty-one reached the cluster-wide threshold marginally, but all were attenuated by adjustment for rs35705950 and none reached it after adjustment (Supplementary Table S5).

text.text: This is a power-limited negative.

Taking the effect sizes and allele frequencies Kousathanas et al. report for the eight mucin-cluster 11p15.5 signals, this sample has 74% power to detect their most strongly associated MUC5B signal (OR 1.71 at a frequency of 0.20) at the cluster-wide threshold but 1% to 2% power for each of the four MUC2 and MUC6 signals, whose odds ratios are 1.15 to 2.10 at allele frequencies of 0.007 to 0.69 (Methods).
The absence of those signals here is therefore uninformative.
We tested whether MUC5AC or MUC5B haplogroup is associated with IPF independently of the MUC5B promoter variant rs35705950 in a dedicated IPF case-control study.
MUC5AC H3 was associated with IPF, but the association is largely explained by its linkage disequilibrium with rs35705950, as was that of MUC5B H1.
A residual MUC5AC H2 association survived adjustment in this cohort but did not replicate in a larger independent sample.

Adjusting rs35705950 for H3 barely changes the rs35705950 estimate (OR 4.03 to 3.90), whereas adjusting H3 for rs35705950 abolishes the H3 estimate (1.63 to 1.10); adding H3 to a model already containing rs35705950 does not improve fit (χ²₁=0.41, p=0.52), whereas the reverse does (χ²₁=77.8, p=1.2×10⁻¹⁸).
This pattern is consistent with the H3 association being explained by rs35705950, or by variation more closely tagged by rs35705950 than by the H3 proxy.

The LD between them (r=0.36) is the key interpretive constraint: because H3 and rs35705950 are co-inherited, no sample of this size can say whether an H3 association reflects VNTR length, rs35705950mediated expression, or another co-inherited variant.

That LD was also addressed directly rather than only by adjustment: nearly a third of participants are discordant for H3 and T carrier status, and the non-carrier stratum removes the promoter variant's variance entirely, where H3 remained directionally consistent but imprecise (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.79-1.69, on 151 cases).
The limit there is power, not LD.
The tag itself is not the limitation, since it indexes H3 at r²=1.0 in Plender's panel and tracks independently imputed repeat length at r=0.98 here.
The joint-model ordering (H2 depleted, H1 intermediate, H3 enriched for the T allele) is what would be seen if risk tracks rs35705950 frequency by haplogroup rather than repeat length.

MUC5AC H2 behaved differently within this cohort: adjustment for rs35705950 did not abolish it (0.58 to 0.69), the estimate was stable across alternative tags and agreed closely with the diplotype complement (r=0.97; Supplementary Table S3), and conditioning on the eight mucin-cluster 11p15.5 signals reported by Kousathanas et al. left the point estimate essentially unchanged, though no longer nominally significant (0.71, p=0.051).

In the independent TOPMed sample the rs35705950-adjusted estimate was null (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.88-1.11), an interval that excludes our estimate, in a sample with five times as many cases, so we do not claim an H2 effect independent of the promoter variant.
The samples differ in control ascertainment and in the men-only composition of IPFJES, but the parsimonious reading is that our estimate was inflated by chance in a small sample.
Whether repeat number itself carries risk can be addressed more directly.

Imputing MUC5AC repeat length into IPFJES from the Bai et al. long-read panel recovered the exon-31 length variants at high fidelity (imputation r²=0.99 for the 751 bp insertion), but imputed length proved equivalent to the clade tag, correlating with H3 count at r=0.98 and carrying the same weak linkage with rs35705950 (r=0.37).
It behaved identically to the H3 tag (unadjusted OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.24-2.07; adjusted 1.06, 0.79-1.41), and a composite of total exon-31 length gave the same result (Supplementary Table S4).

text.text: The MUC5B H1 inverse association (0.71) is explained as H3's is: H2, the predominant MUC5B haplogroup, carries rs35705950 T, making H1 appear protective by contrast, and the estimate attenuates on adjustment (0.82, p=0.25).
Strengths include validated tSNPs from long-read sequencing and a cohort recruited specifically for IPF, with MDT-confirmed diagnoses.
The principal limitation is that array-based tSNPs index a phylogenetic clade within an LD block, so even a surviving association identifies the clade, not the feature driving it.

The second concerns the variants themselves: per-variant imputation quality for the tagging SNPs could not be assessed beyond the r²≥0.5 QC threshold, so imputation error in a tag propagates into haplogroup assignment, and Plender's tagging r² values are averaged across a 206-haplotype panel assembled from 104 individuals, only 10 of them European, so they carry no guarantee of transferring to a European cohort.
The third concerns rs35705950.

It lies within the same locus as the haplogroups and in partial linkage disequilibrium with them, so it is not an external covariate: adjusting for it may remove part of the haplogroup signal itself, and the adjusted estimate asks whether haplogroup matters among chromosomes already matched on promoter genotype, which is a narrower question than whether haplogroup matters at all.

The fourth is power: where an association attenuates, this sample cannot exclude a modest residual (the adjusted MUC5AC H3 interval, 0.83-1.45, remains compatible with a per-allele OR of about 1.45), though pooled with TOPMed it narrows to 0.96 (0.87-1.07).
IPFJES recruited men only, so applicability to women is unknown.
MUC5AC H3 and MUC5B H1 are associated with IPF risk in directions consistent with their LD with rs35705950, and neither association is separable from it.

A MUC5AC H2 association did survive adjustment for rs35705950 here, but was not replicated in an independent sample with five times as many cases, where the rs35705950-adjusted es-timate was null (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.88-1.11).
We therefore do not claim a haplogroup effect independent of the promoter variant.

Only MUC5AC H3 shows appreciable LD with rs35705950, and the IPFJES-controls value (r²=0.10) is consistent with the reference (0.10), indicating the LD is representative rather than a feature of this cohort; the full-sample estimates are modestly larger because cases are enriched for risk haplotypes.
H1, H2 and MUC5B H1 have little LD with rs35705950: r² is 0.02 or less in the controls and 0.06 or less in the full sample, the largest being MUC5AC H2 at 0.06.

Repeat lengths were imputed into the 771 analytical participants from the Bai et al. (2026) long-read VNTR reference panel using the ImputeSV server (BCFtools QC → SHAPEIT5 v5.0.1 phasing → Minimac4 v4.1.6); the 751 bp allele is the exon-31 length variant that tracks the H3 clade in long-read assemblies.
Imputation r² is the server's estimate.

The composite is total inserted exon-31 sequence per participant relative to GRCh38, summed across imputed alleles (r²≥0.30); results are unchanged if built from the two common well-imputed alleles alone (r=0.96 between definitions).
Adding H3 to a model containing the imputed length, or vice versa, does not improve fit (likelihood-ratio p=0.24 and 0.76): the imputed length and the clade tag are the same information.

The imputed length therefore behaves as the H3 tag does, associated unadjusted and abolished by rs35705950, consistent with the paper's argument that an SNPimputed length inherits the tags' linkage disequilibrium and cannot isolate the repeat.
Models adjust for age, ever-smoking, PC1-5 and recruitment centre.

text.text: Every common, well-imputed VNTR and structural-variant allele in the mucin cluster was tested against IPF by logistic regression (adjusted for age, ever-smoking, PC1-5 and recruitment centre), marginally and with rs35705950 T-allele count added; loci present in both the VNTR and SV panels were de-duplicated and kept at their higher imputation r².

The strong marginal associations, concentrated in the MUC2 VNTR domain that no haplogroup analysis reaches, all reflect linkage disequilibrium with rs35705950 (top hits r=0.24-0.53 with the T allele) and are markedly attenuated by adjustment for it (the strongest, a MUC2 allele, from OR 2.77 to 1.64); none survives the cluster-wide threshold, and the smallest adjusted p is within chance expectation across the correlated tests.
Survival of adjustment would in any case not establish a causal repeat effect, since every variant lies in the same linkage-disequilibrium block (Discussion).
Within this sample, then, no imputed mucin structural variant reached significance independently of the promoter variant.

(The MUC5AC H2 haplogroup tags are SNPs, not structural variants, and so are not among the 109 alleles scanned here; the smallest adjusted p in this table, 0.003, is a MUC2 allele at the low end of the common range scanned, whereas the residual H2 association discussed in the main text is assessed against a different, less stringent multiplicity family, the four primary haplogroup coefficients, not this 54-test cluster-wide threshold.)

This is a power-limited negative, not a claim that no such variant exists: in a far larger IPF meta-analysis, GCTA-COJO resolves conditionally-independent signals annotated by nearest gene to MUC2 (three) and MUC6 (one), as well as several in MUC5B (Kousathanas et al., 2025), which 385 cases are underpowered to detect (MUC2 and MUC6 are canonically gastrointestinal mucins, so these labels are positional and need not imply an airway role for those proteins).
